claims.text: A predictive framework can independently calculate lattice and electronic thermal conductivities for HfNbTaTiZr.
Separating lattice and electronic transport will reduce mean absolute prediction error by roughly 30% relative to preceding analytical predictions.
The initial material is defect-free, polycrystalline, bulk HfNbTaTiZr.
An oxygen concentration below 1 wt.% represents a high-purity HfNbTaTiZr condition.
DFT-derived elastic properties can inform temperature-dependent phonon calculations while electronic heat transport is treated separately.
The proposed model is applicable from approximately 200 K to 1200 K.
Below 200 K, lattice and electronic thermal-conductivity contributions in HfNbTaTiZr are comparable.
Separating vibrational modes from free-electron contributions accounts for their distinct scattering processes in the alloy matrix.
Previous models used a single effective Debye temperature and thereby oversimplified transport in HfNbTaTiZr.
Separate lattice and electronic modeling better captures alloy scattering and oxygen-impurity effects in refractory high-entropy alloys.
The predicted total thermal conductivity will agree with measurements within ±15% throughout 200–1200 K.
The model will reproduce comparable lattice and electronic contributions below 200 K.
HfNbTaTiZr specimens containing approximately 1 wt.% oxygen exhibit total thermal conductivity of 10–17 W/(K m) at high temperatures.
Oxygen-containing specimens have lower thermal conductivity than the relevant comparison condition.
Previous predictive approaches primarily used a Debye-temperature effective medium for perfect, defect-free crystals.
Previous approaches deviated from HfNbTaTiZr experiments by more than 30%, particularly when lattice and electronic contributions were not separated.
The hypothesis may not apply when grain-boundary or defect scattering is extensive.
Oxygen content and unmodeled microstructural variation can change the magnitude of the expected improvement.
Electron-phonon coupling in these complex alloys is weak.
Failure to obtain approximately a 30% error reduction against earlier models, or substantial disagreement with experimentally inferred component separation, would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The stated applicability and experimental measurement range begins at 200 K, but the hypothesis also requires validation and reproduction of behavior below 200 K. A 200–1200 K experiment cannot test the claimed sub-200 K behavior.
